question: Which team won the video captioning track of the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (ILSVRC) 2016?
reader_goal: Resolve the premise accurately and directly; identify the relevant 2016 video task without inventing a winning captioning team.

sources.title: Official ILSVRC 2016 challenge page
sources.passage: The official introduction enumerates five challenge tasks: object localization, object detection, object detection from video, scene classification, and scene parsing. It lists no video captioning task.

sources.title: Official ILSVRC 2016 results
sources.passage: The provided-data video detection Task 3a table puts NUIST first with 10 object categories won and mean average precision 0.808292. The detection-and-tracking Task 3c table puts CUVideo first at mean average precision 0.558557. These are separate video detection subtasks, neither a captioning task.

fact_targets.proposition: There was no ILSVRC 2016 video captioning track or winner to name.
The 2016 video task was object detection from video, rather than video captioning.

question: Is SWE-bench Verified still a trustworthy measure of coding-agent progress?
reader_goal: Decide how much weight to place on current SWE-bench Verified scores when assessing coding-agent progress, with a qualified conclusion and attention to competing evidence.

sources.title: OpenAI's August 2024 SWE-bench Verified announcement
sources.passage: OpenAI and the SWE-bench authors released a human-reviewed subset of 500 problems from the original SWE-bench test set, screening issue descriptions and tests for problematic cases. This describes the benchmark's original intended improvement, not current validity.

sources.title: OpenAI's February 2026 reappraisal
sources.passage: OpenAI reports that 59.4 percent of its selected audit of 138 problems had material test or description issues; it also found frontier models reproducing some reference patches or task specifics, a contamination signal. OpenAI stopped reporting Verified scores and recommends another benchmark. The audited subset was selected from tasks a model often failed, so the 59.4 percent is not a prevalence estimate for all 500 tasks.

sources.title: METR's maintainer review study
sources.passage: METR reports that roughly half of test-passing agent patches in its sample would not be merged by maintainers after adjustment for reviewer noise. The study covered 95 issues in three of the benchmark's twelve repositories and did not let agents revise patches after review; its result cautions against equating a passing benchmark score with real-world usefulness.

fact_targets.proposition: SWE-bench Verified began as a 500-problem human-screened subset of SWE-bench.
OpenAI's later selected audit found material test or issue-description problems; the audit percentage must not be presented as prevalence across all 500 tasks.
OpenAI identified evidence of exposure to benchmark solutions and stopped reporting Verified scores.
METR found a substantial gap between automated test passing and maintainer acceptance, with sampling and no-revision limits.
